overview: The Irish (Chicago) Gambit starts with 3.Nxe5 Nxe5 4.d4, when White gives a knight for a pawn and then tries to regain it with a fork on e5. After 4...Ng6 5.e5 or 4...Nc6 5.d5 White has a space advantage and active pieces, but with correct play Black keeps the extra piece and consolidates. It is a rarity, tactically interesting at club level.

white_ideas.idea: Play d4 to attack the knight on e5, gain space with e5 and develop the bishops quickly
Aim at Bc4, Qh5 or Qd2 and a rapid attack on the kingside

black_ideas.idea: Take the knight, retreat it to g6 or c6, and develop calmly
Return material only if needed, then use the extra piece in the endgame

typical_structures.structure: White pawn centre on d4/e4 with Black a knight up and a loosened kingside

character.notes: White sacrifices a piece for central control and initiative; tactics decide. Sharp.

gambit.notes: After 3.Nxe5 Nxe5 4.d4 White has given a knight for a pawn and Black can keep it.

soundness.notes: Considered unsound; Black can consolidate against accurate play.

structure.notes: Open lines and rapid development in the centre; Open.

approach.notes: Seldom chosen by strong players; a surprise weapon.

level.notes: Dubious lines are never Beginner; both sides need tactical precision. Intermediate.

character.reason: A piece sacrifice for an attack; tactical from move three.
